newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus says Russia union deal "all-encompassing".
newsitem.headline: Belarus says Russia union deal "all-encompassing".

text.p: A treaty of union due for signature next month by presidents Alexander Lukashenko of Belarus and Boris Yeltsin of Russia will be "all-encompassing", an aide to the Belarus leader said on Friday.

"An all-encompassing deal is to be signed, foreseeing dual citizenship and a corresponding document. It is too soon to say if this will be a passport or something else," Ivan Pashkevich, Lukashenko's aide on ideology, told a news conference.
"The agreement significantly broadens the rights of the parliamentary assembly," Pashkevich, who is the deputy head of Lukashenko's administration, added.
He said these powers could involve direct elections to the assembly, which currently groups 25 deputies from each of the two countries' parliaments.
The assembly was created on April 2 last year, the day Lukashenko and Yeltsin signed a "commonwealth" deal which has drawn vigorous opposition from nationalists in Belarus.
The two men are due to meet again exactly a year later to sign a new deal, heralding even closer ties.
Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko, speaking to reporters in Moscow, said on Friday the deal provides for a union of independent states rather than a federation.
